feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant platforms, and solid scope. It reads professionally, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in leadership roles with increasing scope, budget/governance ownership, and technical depth.  
- Good credibility through concrete scale indicators: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms.  
- Writing is polished and audience-appropriate, with strong positioning around digital strategy, advocacy communications, and cross-functional leadership.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond scope: e.g., traffic growth, email engagement, conversion improvements, production savings, team size, or campaign results. Several bullets describe responsibilities more than achievements.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience”; keep serial comma usage consistent (“workflows and systems” vs. “workflows, and systems”); “French (A2/Learning)” is slightly awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with one or two concrete signals of seniority and more emphasis on recent leadership in digital transformation.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with current value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications leadership for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with tighter phrasing like “multi-channel digital communications.”
- Add specificity tied to recent roles, e.g., “enterprise web modernization,” “editorial governance,” or “analytics-informed communications.”

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading multi-channel communications, enterprise web modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, editorial workflows, stakeholder coordination, and platform governance, with a strong track record translating technical and policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and “stakeholder coordination” are already reinforced in Core Competencies and Soft Skills.
- The channel list overlaps with multiple experience bullets and could be condensed.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership/strategy capabilities will make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Multi-channel communications,” not “communication.”
- Prioritize strategic/leadership competencies over task-level items like “Web & CMS administration.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Enterprise web & CMS modernization • Editorial workflow & content operations • Cross-channel communications leadership • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Workflow systems & governance • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Consider replacing “Workflow & systems architecture” with “Workflow systems & governance” for clearer business relevance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- Several items overlap with Topline Skills; if that section stays, keep this block shorter and more high-level.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and project section. Tighten it around 3–5 high-impact outcomes and make the freelance/full-time nature feel more senior and strategic.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership language: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate into fewer bullets focused on outcomes, e.g.:
- Led Drupal-based campaign and storytelling builds, including microsites, modular content components, and member-facing resource hubs.
- Built digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve cross-channel communications across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Directed AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content model, and user discovery experience.
- Add metrics if possible: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, or workflow time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI-enabled search and microsite details already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level.
- Governance/analytics/platform modernization also overlap with the NACo role and headline summary.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were more concise and if channel management bullets emphasized outcomes, not just scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget strategy for a national membership organization.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Recast channel bullet to show business value: add engagement, growth, campaign support, or audience reach if available; otherwise shorten to avoid a generic responsibilities line.
- Combine operations/analytics language for concision: “Built reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery while formalizing governance, publishing standards, and cross-department workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role’s day-to-day channel management; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with “Advocacy Video Series” in Recent Projects; keep one focused on infrastructure, the other on programming.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and currently reads as support-oriented rather than impact-driven. Tighten it to emphasize scope, ownership, and what expanded under your leadership in this period.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for a national public-sector audience.”
- Replace “helping” language with ownership verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands…”; “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger operations bullet: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows by coordinating communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency across digital channels.”
- Add any measurable outcomes if available: newsletter open/click rates, video cadence/views, publishing volume, stakeholder teams supported, or workflow time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier NACo role and the Recent Projects section; distinguish this as expansion/operationalization, not initial creation.
- “Publishing workflows/editorial coordination” also overlaps with the Director role; keep this version focused on execution rather than governance.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/freelance experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and avoid generic phrasing like “audience-focused content planning.”

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for sharper executive-level positioning:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Content strategy for complex stakeholder audiences
- Consider replacing “messaging” with “communications” to sound more strategic and less tactical.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this area to scale from recent roles (e.g., 10,000+ page platform, 50+ publishers, millions of annual page views) rather than keeping it purely generic.
- Keep wording parallel: noun-based phrases, no mixed styles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with Core Competencies; consider swapping in “content operations” or “stakeholder communications.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capabilities and recent strengths rather than repeat software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from platforms list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items like “jQuery” unless central to target roles; it dates the profile.
- Consider replacing “WordPress - SharePoint - Power Pages” with “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint and Power Pages” to reduce bullet fragmentation.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere, such as “enterprise CMS modernization” or “large public-facing web properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost exactly; keep Topline Skills broader and save full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies; avoid repeating all three verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics capability over listing every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting.”
- Consolidate tools into one phrase instead of a long list: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity.”
- Tighten and modernize wording: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboards and decision support.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive dashboards and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Since recent NACo experience already proves these tools, avoid repeating the exact same platform list elsewhere unless this section is shortened.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to the in-house studio and event delivery leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery**

- Keep terms parallel and concise; “video production and editing” is broad, while “broadcast-quality” and “in-house studio production” better reflect recent leadership impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the Core Competencies line **“Multimedia production and livestream operations.”** Consider consolidating or differentiating this item toward **studio/event systems** specifically.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” and “Livestreaming” partially overlap; combine to avoid repetition.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. Since Drupal is central to recent roles, this item should emphasize depth/order rather than just naming tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider adding light qualifiers to show level: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make it outcome-oriented: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; campaign microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Keep formatting parallel and concise; avoid mixing CMS names with broader capabilities here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills entry; consider trimming one or using this section for tools only and the topline section for broader capabilities.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor versus the seniority of the CV unless it supports a specific recent project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from basic languages to applied capability: “Front-end implementation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group tools by function for clarity: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- Keep only tools you actively use in recent roles/projects; if GTM is important, specify outcome-oriented use: “Google Tag Manager implementation”
- Suggested rewrite: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- “API integrations” and workflow/technical execution themes also overlap with Core Competencies and Topline Skills; this section should stay tool-specific.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools.”
- Group by function to improve scanability: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Team collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work: “used to support editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and process automation.”
- Keep only tools you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; cut weaker/older platforms if they dilute credibility.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.
- Slack and Teams are very common; consider dropping one or both unless they support a specific systems narrative.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory rather than evidence of capability. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize systems breadth, not repeat newsletter management.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/strength: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add functional scope instead of just names: **Higher Logic (member email/community engagement) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey orchestration, segmentation) • Mailchimp (campaign deployment)**
- Keep to platforms only; avoid adding outcomes here unless you can tie them directly to hands-on administration or implementation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in recent work experience.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications language elsewhere, so keep this item platform-specific.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts” and concrete contributions rather than general team support.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted through two digital roles as part of NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten and specify contributions: “Supported web, email, social and multimedia operations; helped improve publishing workflows and cross-channel coordination.”
- Clarify standout outputs: “Contributed to a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email volume, or team size supervised.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; in this item, frame it as launching or early production support if accurate.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is repeated elsewhere; keep this version more junior and execution-oriented.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or “firsts,” while keeping scope modest relative to more senior NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize initiative and ownership: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy communications.”
- Split the multimedia work into a clearer impact statement: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational campaigns and member-facing materials.”
- Make the podcast achievement the anchor: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If you can, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience/downloads, stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad phrases like “digital content production” if later NACo roles already cover multimedia extensively; keep this entry focused on research/innovation support plus the podcast first.
- Don’t overstate leadership here, since later roles more credibly show team and channel ownership.
